macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stock futures rebound ahead of major earnings
items.summary: Dow futures rose about 0.2%, S&P 500 futures 0.6%, and Nasdaq 100 futures 1.2% on Monday after last week’s sell-off, as investors focused on upcoming results from Tesla, Meta, Netflix, American Express, and GE Aerospace.[2]

items.title: Wall Street ends sharply lower after technology-led sell-off
items.summary: In Friday’s session, the S&P 500 fell 1.09%, the Nasdaq-100 dropped 2.5%, the Dow declined 0.34%, and the Russell 2000 lost 1.66%. The Nasdaq-100 fell more than 5% for the week amid concerns about AI-related financing and valuations.[3]

items.title: Markets reduce expectations for an October Fed rate hike
items.summary: Traders priced an 85.1% probability that the Federal Reserve will leave rates unchanged at its October meeting, up from 42.4% a month earlier. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh offered no specific policy guidance while officials remain in the pre-meeting blackout period.[2]

items.title: Hotter industrial output and elevated oil prices remain key macro risks
items.summary: Market commentary highlighted stronger-than-expected industrial output and inflation that remains too high but broadly in line with expectations. Brent crude held above $107 a barrel, adding to concerns about inflation and interest-rate policy.[4]

items.title: Busy earnings week to test investor confidence
items.summary: Major companies scheduled to report this week include GE Aerospace, 3M, General Motors, Netflix, Meta, Tesla, IBM, and Texas Instruments. Investors are watching whether earnings can offset concerns over technology valuations and AI investment financing.[1]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: JPMorgan deploys JPM Coin on Ethereum
items.summary: JPMorgan confirmed that its JPM Coin, representing dollar deposits, is now available to eligible institutional customers on Ethereum, expanding the bank’s blockchain payments infrastructure.

items.title: Bitcoin trades around $82,000–$83,000 as crypto market edges higher
items.summary: Bitcoin rebounded above $83,000 in some market data, while reports showed the broader crypto market up modestly over 24 hours. Ethereum remained near $2,400 and continued to underperform Bitcoin over the past week.

items.title: CFTC proposes voluntary unified federal oversight for crypto exchanges
items.summary: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission proposed a Reg CM framework that would let crypto exchanges opt into federal oversight instead of managing fragmented state licensing requirements.

items.title: EU reviews MiCA staking rules
items.summary: The European Commission’s MiCA review is examining whether existing staking regulations are adequate, potentially leading to additional requirements for companies offering staking services.

items.title: Strive buys about $100 million of Bitcoin
items.summary: Strive disclosed purchases of approximately 1,223 BTC between October 14 and 16, raising its Bitcoin holdings to 36,818 BTC.

items.title: Bitmine adds 12,535 ETH to treasury
items.summary: Bitmine reported acquiring 12,535 ETH during the previous week, bringing its holdings to 6,041,481 ETH, with more than 5 million ETH committed to staking.

items.title: Coinbase and Thunes announce stablecoin payments partnership
items.summary: Coinbase plans to use Thunes’ international payments network to deliver funds to local bank accounts and mobile wallets, while Thunes will access Coinbase’s stablecoin infrastructure.

items.title: Mastercard launches stablecoin transaction screening service
items.summary: Mastercard introduced Stablecoin Security, a service intended to help payment providers screen on-chain transactions for fraud, scams and sanctions exposure before funds move.

items.title: Qubic reports exploit affecting 1,404 wallets
items.summary: Qubic said attackers exploited inadequate randomness in wallet seed generation to drain approximately 2.94 trillion QU from 1,404 wallets, while stating that the core protocol was not the source of the flaw.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: DeepSeek releases V4.1-Flash-1017 open-weight model
items.summary: DeepSeek announced V4.1-Flash-1017, an MIT-licensed model update focused on faster, leaner agentic coding. The company reports improvements across 11 benchmarks, including a 77.0 score on DeepSWE, along with new Search and Fetch APIs; the reported results have not been independently verified.

items.title: Meta launches Muse AI model family
items.summary: Meta reportedly launched Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, describing them as its most capable AI models, and introduced Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter open coding model trained on NVIDIA GB300 systems.

items.title: Anthropic proposes public-interest fund
items.summary: Anthropic announced plans to place an initial 5% of the company’s shares into a public-interest fund, subject to shareholder approval, with potential additions tied to future valuation increases.

items.title: Mistral releases Timestral forecasting models
items.summary: Mistral AI released Timestral, a time-series foundation-model family ranging from 5 million to 209 million parameters. The largest model is reported to outperform competing zero-shot forecasting systems on several evaluations and is designed to run on CPUs.

items.title: Google open-sources Harness² for improving AI-agent performance
items.summary: Google Research reportedly open-sourced Harness², a method for recursively improving the software harness surrounding a fixed AI model without ground-truth verifiers. Reported experiments showed substantial gains on the WorkBuddy-Bench benchmark.

items.title: Google expands Gemini 4 Argon availability
items.summary: Google reportedly made Gemini 4 Argon available across selected business and developer products, with introductory token pricing announced through November 30, 2026.

items.title: Google releases EmbeddingGemma 2 for on-device multimodal search
items.summary: Google reportedly launched EmbeddingGemma 2, a 740-million-parameter embedding model that maps text, images, audio and video into a shared representation for local search and retrieval.

items.title: AI agents and enterprise deployment remain major industry trends
items.summary: Recent announcements highlight a shift from AI pilots toward scaled enterprise deployments, including Cognizant’s planned rollout of Claude to roughly 350,000 employees and growing investment in agentic AI infrastructure and workplace skills.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox seeks physical-games supply strategist
items.summary: Microsoft is hiring an Xbox Games Supply Strategist to coordinate physical game launches and distribution, suggesting Xbox intends to maintain support for physical releases despite the industry’s shift toward digital sales.

items.title: Xbox executive highlights widespread AI use in game development
items.summary: Microsoft Xbox executive Brandon Stirrup said studios are broadly using AI despite negative sentiment among gamers. His comments, shared on social media, reportedly went viral before the account became inactive.

items.title: Esports World Cup expands 2027 qualification framework
items.summary: The Esports Foundation announced a qualification system for the 2027 Esports World Cup that will incorporate third-party tournament organizers and grassroots venues.

items.title: FURIA wins Thunderpick World Championship
items.summary: FURIA defeated BetBoom 3–2 in Malta to claim its second Thunderpick World Championship title and end an almost year-long trophy drought.

items.title: LOUD reaches Champions Shanghai grand final
items.summary: LOUD defeated Team Vitality 2–1 after a disputed round rollback to reach its first international championship final since 2022.

items.title: Steam reaches new concurrent-user record
items.summary: Steam reportedly surpassed 43.5 million simultaneous users, exceeding its previous March 2026 record of 42,686,616 concurrent users.

items.title: Liquid Swords declares bankruptcy
items.summary: Independent studio Liquid Swords reportedly filed for bankruptcy after months of being unable to pay employee salaries.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 enters campaign early access
items.summary: Digital preorders for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 provide campaign early access from October 16, with the full release scheduled for October 23 on PC, Xbox Series, PlayStation 5, and Nintendo Switch 2.
